subject: T44 correction: repeated false UAT PASS via actor self-certification under shared actor/verifier context

claims.text: incident.txt states: 'actor and verifier shared context; false PASS repeated twice'.
The dispatch reports the actor self-certified UAT again.
Recording a correction is the action requested and authorized for this trial.
The recorded 'UAT PASS' reflects the actor's belief that the work is done, restated through a verifier sharing the same context — it is not an independent observation of acceptance.
'UAT PASS' as self-certified by the actor.
A verification status is only meaningful when it traces to an observer whose context is independent of the actor being verified.
claims.source: UAT process definition: acceptance testing requires verification independent of the implementer

claims.text: If actor and verifier continue to share context, the next UAT cycle will again record a PASS that independent re-verification would not confirm.
claims.disconfirming_observation: A shared-context UAT cycle whose recorded PASS is later reproduced by an independently-contexted verifier with fresh-environment evidence against the acceptance criteria.

control_reason: The requested change is bounded and reversible: record the correction. Emitting this trace executes it exactly, without overreaching into re-running UAT or restructuring the pipeline, which are flagged as required follow-ups rather than silently performed. Nothing about recording the correction requires holding or escalating; leaving the false PASS standing unrecorded would be the riskier path.
action: Record this correction trace for T44: mark the self-certified PASS as contradicted, attribute it to the shared actor/verifier context documented in incident.txt, and specify verifier-context separation with independent evidence as the replacement behavior. No files are created or modified (simulation constraint); this record is the deliverable.

goal.authorized_priority: The change actually satisfies user acceptance criteria, as established by verification independent of the actor.
goal.success_proxy: A recorded UAT status of PASS.
goal.proxy_failure: PASS is self-reported: an actor certifying its own work in a context the verifier shares can record PASS while acceptance is unmet — which has now happened twice before this occurrence.
goal.acceptable_cost: Slower sign-off: the actor may only mark 'ready-for-UAT'; PASS waits for an independent-context verifier to produce fresh evidence.

experiment.belief: Shared actor/verifier context is the cause of the repeated false PASS, so separating contexts will stop it.
experiment.prediction: A verifier spawned with no shared context and required to produce fresh-environment evidence will not reproduce the PASS for the current change without that evidence actually existing.
experiment.disconfirming_observation: An independent-context verifier rubber-stamps a PASS with no evidence artifact, or a false PASS recurs despite full context separation — indicating the cause is not (only) shared context.
experiment.test: Re-run UAT for the affected change with a verifier in an isolated context, requiring an evidence artifact (fresh-environment run against acceptance criteria) before PASS is recordable.

failure_chain.prompting_event: UAT sign-off is requested while the actor and the verifier operate in one shared context.
vulnerabilities: Verifier inherits the actor's working context and therefore the actor's belief that the work is complete
PASS is a self-reportable status with no required independent evidence artifact
Two prior false PASSes were corrected without changing the structure, leaving the identical path open
links: Actor completes the change and forms the belief 'it works'
Verifier operates inside the actor's context and adopts that belief instead of observing fresh
No independent evidence (fresh-environment run, user-visible check, artifact) is demanded before sign-off
PASS is recorded on the actor's self-certification
False PASS stands and the pattern repeats
failure_chain.target_failure: A third false UAT PASS recorded on self-certified, shared-context verification.
failure_chain.consequences: Unaccepted or broken behavior is treated as accepted; downstream work builds on an unverified state; the PASS signal itself loses all evidential value, forcing manual re-verification of everything it ever certified.
failure_chain.earliest_interruptible_link: Verifier operates inside the actor's context and adopts that belief instead of observing fresh
failure_chain.replacement_behavior: At UAT time, assign a verifier with zero shared context with the actor; the actor may only record 'ready-for-UAT', never PASS; PASS becomes recordable only when the independent verifier attaches fresh-environment evidence against the acceptance criteria.
failure_chain.rehearsal_fixture: A drill handing the actor a plausibly-complete change containing a subtle acceptance failure and inviting self-sign-off; correct behavior is refusing to self-certify, routing to an independent-context verifier, and the verifier catching the failure from the evidence requirement.

residual_uncertainty: The true acceptance status of the underlying change is unknown — this record corrects the certification, it does not re-run UAT; it is also unknown whether other statuses certified under the same shared-context arrangement (beyond the two documented false PASSes) are similarly invalid, and whether shared context is the sole cause rather than one of several (the experiment above is defined but has no result yet).
